market_holds: The quarter itself is already out. On 2026-11-03 Opera pre-announced Q3: revenue $182.8M (+20% y/y, top of the $181-183M guide), adj. EBITDA $43.2M (above the $41-43M range), query +17%, advertising +22%, and 100M desktop MAU in October (6-K ex99.1). The stock rose 4.46% that day. That leaves Q4 guidance, the full-year update, 2027 tone, Google renewal news and capital returns for tomorrow. The CFO said the late date lets them 'approach our final Q4 guidance with our typical prudence'. FY26 guide is $734-742M. Year to date is $536.7M, so the guide implies Q4 of $197.3-205.3M (+11.5% to +16.1% y/y on ~$177M, midpoint +13.8%). StockAnalysis FY26 consensus, updated Nov 4, is $740.0M (7 analysts), which implies Q4 of about $203.3M (+14.9%), a bit above the guide midpoint. FY27 consensus is $853M (+15%). Every rating is Buy, with an average target of $26.29 against spot $15.43. The price has fallen hard: -12.5% over 20 days and -17.8% since Oct 28, against QQQ -8.6% and IWM -3.0%. The break came with Alphabet's Q3 on Oct 28 (GOOGL -12.6% on Oct 29; OPRA -6.8% that day and -11.3% the next) and with a Nasdaq drawdown (QQQ -2.4% today). It was not Opera's own news. Market cap is about $1.37B (88.9M shares), with about $145M cash at Q2, roughly 7x FY26 EBITDA guide and a 5.2% dividend yield. The options chain is unusable for a move (ATM spread 104% of mid), but call wings are bid over puts (25d skew -15.6 vol points) and the front-week ATM IV is 103%. Short interest was last seen at about 1.6M shares, 4.5 days to cover (June 30, stale). Prior full-release reactions: Q3'25 -3.4%, Q4'25 +23.4% (2026 guide plus $300M buyback), Q1'26 +5.3%, Q2'26 -7.1% (beat and raise, but a decelerating Q3 guide).
view: Q3 is known, so the print turns on the Q4 guide and what comes with it. On numbers the guide most likely lands close to consensus. Opera raises the FY by about the size of each beat (midpoint 727.5 -> 733.5 -> 738), and the Q3 beat was only +$0.8M against the guide midpoint. A Q4 guide near $200-205M is the base case, roughly $203M street, with the CFO's 'prudence' line tilting it toward the low side of that. Last year's Q4 guide ($162-165M) was beaten by 8% at the midpoint, and management said in August it builds in a 'more normalized Q4 spike'. The street knows that habit, though. The Aug 19 reaction (-7% on a decelerating guide despite a beat) shows this stock trades on the implied growth rate, and a Q4 of about +13-15% continues that deceleration. The upside paths are a Google renewal confirmation (management said in April the renewal falls 'more towards the second half' and expected 'no surprises'), opportunistic buybacks at about $15 against the $17.44 they paid in Q2, a dividend declaration, and a constructive 2027 tone. They could re-rate a stock that sold off about 13 points more than QQQ on Alphabet's print and the tape rather than its own news. The downside path is a prudent Q4 guide that reads as a sub-15% exit rate, plus a still-weak tape. I lean slightly up because the run-in came largely from the tape and from Google, while Opera's own data since then (pre-announcement, 100M desktop MAU) is positive. I cannot see the guide, though, and the evidence does not take me near a confident call.
unpriced: Possibly the part of the -18% since Oct 28 that came from Alphabet's Q3 miss and a Nasdaq drawdown rather than from Opera's own data. Opera's own news over that span was positive (Q3 at the top, desktop MAU +16%). A guide in line with consensus, a Google renewal or a buyback update could close some of that gap. I cannot show this gap is large or that the release will close it inside the window, so it stays a lean.

recommendation.reason: The quarter was pre-announced, so the reaction depends on a Q4 guide I cannot see. The arithmetic puts it near consensus ($201M implied by the FY guide midpoint vs about $203M street), and the CFO flagged 'prudence'. The run-in is mostly tape and Alphabet sympathy, which gives a mild upward lean, but nothing reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide whose midpoint is at or below about $200M (FY held at or narrowed below $740M), read as an exit rate under 14%, would make the release negative. A confirmed Google renewal plus a FY raise above $742M would make it clearly positive.

self_critique: The lean up rests on the idea that a tape-driven sell-off mean-reverts on an in-line release. With a decelerating-growth stock, a CFO explicitly pre-signalling a prudent Q4 guide, a street Q4 above the guide midpoint and a weak Nasdaq tape, the asymmetric risk may be down, as on Aug 19 (-7%). Equally, Opera's record of low-balled Q4 guides and a possible buyback at depressed prices could make a large up move (as in Feb, +23%). Both cases are plausible, which is why I make no call.
approach_notes: P6 (take the run-in apart) helped most: setting OPRA beside GOOGL, QQQ and IWM showed the drop was not this company's news. P7's push to estimate the hidden guide from its inputs was workable here (the FY guide less YTD), but the guide sits too close to consensus to give a direction.
